final_note: You harnessed the exponential power of T on rate.

concepts.def: Frequency factor; collisions of right geometry.
Energy distribution of molecules at T.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Take ln of both sides: ln k = ln A - Ea/(RT). Plot ln k vs 1/T.

Gradient = -Ea/R, so Ea = -gradient × R (R = 8.31 J/K/mol). Intercept = ln A.

walkthroughs.h2: Why small T rises boost rate
walkthroughs.body_html:
The Maxwell-Boltzmann curve shifts so the fraction with E >= Ea grows exponentially.

A 10 K rise can roughly double rate for typical Ea values around 50 kJ/mol near room temperature.

Catalyst lowers Ea, so a larger area under the Boltzmann curve has E >= Ea. Concentration and shape of curve unchanged.

Enzymes and transition metals (heterogeneous) commonly act this way.
